import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 94

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/94](https://www.erdosproblems.com/94)
- [Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*. Eureka
  (1992), 44-48.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős, I
  (1997), 47-67.
- [LeTh95] Lefmann, Hanno and Thiele, Torsten, *Point sets with distinct distances*. Combinatorica
  (1995), 379-408.
-/

open Filter EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos94

/-- The regular $n$-gon inscribed in the unit circle. -/
noncomputable def regularNGon (n : ℕ) : Finset ℝ² :=
  (Finset.range n).image fun k : ℕ =>
    !₂[Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * k / n), Real.sin (2 * Real.pi * k / n)]

/--
Suppose $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ determine a convex polygon and the set of distances between
them is $\{u_1,\ldots,u_t\}$. Suppose $u_i$ appears as the distance between $f(u_i)$ many pairs of
points. Then
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3.$$

In [Er97c] Erdős claims that Fishburn solved this, but gives no reference.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos94.lean"]
theorem erdos_94 : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ P : Finset ℝ², ConvexIndep (P : Set ℝ²) →
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ C * (P.card : ℝ) ^ 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Note it is trivial that $\sum f(u_i)=\binom{n}{2}$.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_94.variants.sum_multiplicity (P : Finset ℝ²) :
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, distanceMultiplicity P u = P.card.choose 2 := by
  sorry

/--
Lefmann and Theile [LeTh95] prove a stronger version of this question, that
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3$$
under the weaker assumption that no three points are on a line.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_94.variants.no_three_on_a_line : ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ P : Finset ℝ²,
    NonTrilinear (P : Set ℝ²) →
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ C * (P.card : ℝ) ^ 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Fishburn also make the stronger conjecture that $\sum f(u_i)^2$ is maximal for the
regular $n$-gon (for large enough $n$).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_94.variants.regular_ngon : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ P : Finset ℝ²,
    P.card = n → ConvexIndep (P : Set ℝ²) →
    ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, (distanceMultiplicity P u : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤
      ∑ u ∈ distanceSet (regularNGon n), (distanceMultiplicity (regularNGon n) u : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos94

reformulations.difference: The source writes an asymptotic bound ∑ f(u)² ≪ n³; Lean gives one positive constant valid for every finite convex-independent point set, including cardinalities below three.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing E(P) for the sum and n = P.card, the counting identity gives E(P) ≤ (∑ f(u))² = binom(n,2)² ≤ n⁴. Consequently, an eventual bound with constant C for n ≥ N extends to every size using max(C,N): for n < N, n⁴ ≤ N·n³, including the empty case. The converse is immediate. This equivalence was proved without using the file’s sorry theorems as Review94.main_equiv_asymptotic in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The no-three-collinear variant likewise replaces the source’s asymptotic notation with a uniform bound over all finite point sets satisfying that hypothesis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same bound E(P) ≤ P.card⁴ handles every size below an eventual threshold, without any geometric assumption. Increasing the eventual constant to max(C,N) therefore gives exactly the all-size formulation. Proved as Review94.nontri_equiv_asymptotic in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked all five declarations. Independent Lean tests establish exact division by two in distanceMultiplicity, the sum-of-multiplicities identity, empty/singleton/two-point cases, regularNGon’s cardinality and convex independence for every n, and ConvexIndep → NonTrilinear. The regular-polygon comparison uses the correct uniform eventual quantifier and a legitimate unit-circle representative. In /workspace/review/proof-bridge.lean, the cited explicit bound was bridged to the exact main and no-three-collinear theorem types; both proofs depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Two compatibility edits to the older external proof were made only in the scratch copy. Status records agree with the cited website. Access limitation: full texts of Er92e, Er97c, and LeTh95 could not be retrieved; mathematical wording was checked against the website’s exact LaTeX, with the solved bound additionally corroborated by the published abstract and verified formal proof.
